Coordinate Conversion: Translate between geographic coordinates (longitude/latitude) and A5 cell IDs in their numeric or hex string forms. Use these as your entry and exit points for indexing data into A5.
Cell Properties: Inspect a specific cell — its area and average edge length in meters, its resolution level, whether it's a validly-encoded cell, and the polygon vertices that form its boundary. Useful for filtering, validation, and rendering cells on a map.
Hierarchy: Navigate up and down A5's 31-level resolution hierarchy. Roll cells up to a coarser parent for aggregation, expand to children for fine-grained analysis, or compact a set of sibling cells back into their parent.
Traversal: Find cells in a neighborhood: edge- or vertex-adjacent grid disks for fixed-step traversal, or all cells within a metric radius. Use these for proximity queries and spatial joins.
Utilities: General-purpose helpers — total cell count at a resolution, the 12 base cells covering the globe at resolution 0 (and the single root world cell above them), and parent/child cell ratios.
Geometry Integration: Convert cells to and from DuckDB's built-in `GEOMETRY` type — no `spatial` extension dependency required to produce it. Turn a cell into its boundary polygon or center point, or cover an arbitrary point, line, or polygon geometry with cells.
